description: D2: for every mutation the tests missed, is the replacement an equivalent rewrite or a real test gap? Asked per missed mutation by `mutate`; the answers only annotate the result line and mutations.json, never the counts.

equivalent.label: 等价改写
equivalent.instructions: `mutation.new` replaces `mutation.old` at the marked position inside `context`. Judge only whether the replaced code has the same observable behaviour as the original for every input the surrounding code can pass to it: the same return values, the same exceptions, the same side effects. Different wording with the same behaviour is equivalent.

criteria.true: The replacement behaves exactly like the original for every possible input.
criteria.false: Some input makes the replacement behave differently from the original.

untested.label: 测试缺口
untested.instructions: Assume the replacement does change behaviour for some input, and `test_command` still passed with the replacement in place. Judge only whether that means no test reaches the changed behaviour.

criteria.true: The changed behaviour is not exercised by any test, so the test suite cannot notice the change.
criteria.false: The change is equivalent or unobservable from the tests' point of view, so a passing run proves nothing about coverage.
